sentences.zh: 在公众和政治压力不断增加的情况下，罗森斯坦任命了一位外部人士担任特别检察官，一个被认为不依附于任何人的人：罗伯特·穆勒。

sentences.en: Mueller was nominated by George W.
sentences.zh: 穆勒是由乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush in 2001.

sentences.en: Bob Mueller's term in office will last longer than my own, and the next 10 years will bring new forms of crime, new threats of terror from beyond our borders and within them.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·穆勒的任期将比我更长，未来十年将带来新型犯罪，以及来自境外和境内的恐怖主义新威胁。

sentences.en: Went before the Senate for his confirmation hearings.
sentences.zh: 他出席了参议院的确认听证会。

sentences.en: I cannot promise perfection, but I can commit to you and to the dedicated men and women of the FBI that I'll do my very best to earn your faith and your respect.
sentences.zh: 我无法承诺完美，但我可以向你们以及联邦调查局敬业的男女同仁承诺，我会竭尽全力赢得你们的信任和尊重。

sentences.en: Gets confirmed and is sworn in as FBI director on September 4th, 2001.
sentences.zh: 他获得确认，并于2001年9月4日宣誓就任联邦调查局局长。

sentences.en: Okay, so Mueller becomes director of the FBI, and then what happens?
sentences.zh: 好的，穆勒成为了联邦调查局局长，然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: It is in the other building.

sentences.en: We just saw a plane circling the building.

sentences.en: The world changes.
sentences.zh: 世界变了。

sentences.en: And I don't think there's an institution that changed more and certainly more quickly than Bob Mueller's FBI.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有哪个机构比鲍勃·穆勒领导下的联邦调查局改变得更多，也肯定改变得更快。

sentences.en: So how did it change?
sentences.zh: 那么它是如何改变的呢？

sentences.en: Well, overnight it becomes you need to be a counterterrorism organization.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一夜之间，你必须成为一个反恐组织。

sentences.en: You need to be the tip of the spear of our domestic national security.
sentences.zh: 你必须成为我们国内国家安全的最前线。

sentences.en: And the FBI was just not built for that.
sentences.zh: 而联邦调查局根本不是为此而建立的。

sentences.en: This was a crime fighting organization.
sentences.zh: 这原本是一个打击犯罪的组织。

sentences.en: And Mueller's job was help dismantle al-Qaeda, prevent terrorist attacks in the United States, while simultaneously reorganizing and redesigning the very nature of the FBI.
sentences.zh: 穆勒的工作是帮助瓦解基地组织，防止美国境内的恐怖袭击，同时重组和重新设计联邦调查局的本质。

sentences.en: Let me conclude at this juncture by emphasizing again the FBI's total and unwavering commitment to this investigation.
sentences.zh: 在此我再次强调，联邦调查局对这项调查有着全面且坚定不移的承诺。

sentences.en: We will not stop.
sentences.zh: 我们不会停止。

sentences.en: And as I said before, we will leave no stone unturned.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，我们将不遗余力。

sentences.en: Until we have determined who was responsible for these attacks on our freedom.
sentences.zh: 直到我们查明是谁应对这些针对我们自由的袭击负责。

sentences.en: A lot of agents have described it as changing the engine on a plane while you're in the middle of the fight.
sentences.zh: 许多探员将其描述为在战斗中更换飞机的引擎。

sentences.en: And what was Mueller's specific role in changing the FBI after the attack?
sentences.zh: 穆勒在袭击后改变联邦调查局的具体角色是什么？

sentences.en: What did he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: There were a lot of calls, both in Congress and by outside experts, who said, listen, the FBI is just not equipped for this counterterrorism mission.
sentences.zh: 当时国会和外部专家有很多呼声，他们说，听着，联邦调查局根本不具备执行这种反恐任务的能力。

sentences.en: It can't be both a national security organization and a law enforcement organization.
sentences.zh: 它不可能既是一个国家安全组织，又是一个执法组织。

sentences.en: You should split them up and break it into two.
sentences.zh: 你们应该把它们分开，拆成两个机构。

sentences.en: Break it into two.
sentences.zh: 拆成两个。

sentences.en: You know, Mueller did not want us to deal with any of these things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，穆勒不想让我们处理这些事情。

sentences.en: He wanted the Bureau to keep focusing on the job, and he believed that we have a lot of threats going on.
sentences.zh: 他希望局里继续专注于工作，他相信我们面临着很多威胁。

sentences.en: We need to focus on the cases.
sentences.zh: 我们需要专注于案件。

sentences.en: My name is Ali Safan.
sentences.zh: 我叫阿里·萨凡。

sentences.en: I am a former FBI special agent, and I served under Robert Mueller when he was director of the FBI.
sentences.zh: 我曾是一名联邦调查局特别探员，在罗伯特·穆勒担任局长期间曾在其麾下工作。

sentences.en: The reason that Mueller has a mystique about him is he revamps the FBI, he directs the counterterrorism investigations into 9-11 and al-Qaeda,
sentences.zh: 穆勒之所以具有神秘感，是因为他重组了联邦调查局，指挥了针对9·11和基地组织的反恐调查，

sentences.en: and he works Washington and saves the FBI and preserves it as a singular institution.
sentences.zh: 他周旋于华盛顿，拯救了联邦调查局，并将其作为一个独特的机构保存了下来。

sentences.en: He knew what kind of assets he have in the FBI and how to utilize this asset for the benefit of this nation.
sentences.zh: 他知道联邦调查局拥有什么样的资产，以及如何利用这些资产为国家谋利益。

sentences.en: He's such an amazing leader like that.
sentences.zh: 他就是这样一位了不起的领导者。

sentences.en: What was Bob Mueller's leadership style like during this time?
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·穆勒在那段时期的领导风格是怎样的？

sentences.en: And in particular, if you have any examples of it?
sentences.zh: 特别是，你有什么具体的例子吗？

sentences.en: he was personally involved he wasn't the type of director who say okay you know what you uh so and so deal with the day-to-day operation and i'll deal with the strategy
sentences.zh: 他亲力亲为，他不是那种会说‘好吧，你处理日常运作，我来处理战略’的局长。

sentences.en: he uh in a way sometimes micromanaged things you know he wanted to know details about different
sentences.zh: 他在某种程度上甚至会事无巨细地管理，你知道，他想了解各种细节。

sentences.en: things uh he had briefs in the morning and in the evening director's briefs were all the information
sentences.zh: 他每天早晚都有简报，局长简报包含了所有信息，

sentences.en: were, you know, given to him about what's happening on the biggest threats around the nation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，关于全国各地正在发生的最大威胁，都会汇报给他。

sentences.en: So he was really kind of like hands-on individual.
sentences.zh: 所以他真的是一个事必躬亲的人。

sentences.en: He knew everything that was happening in the organization and he put a lot of time and effort, you know, his own time to focus on all these matters.
sentences.zh: 他了解组织内发生的一切，并投入了大量的时间和精力，你知道，他用自己的时间来专注于所有这些事务。

sentences.en: He surrounded himself by people who had a relentless work ethic, didn't require a lot of sleep and were away from their families.
sentences.zh: 他身边围绕着一群工作极其刻苦的人，他们不需要太多睡眠，也远离家人。

sentences.en: And so it wasn't, this was not a touchy-feely time for the FBI.
sentences.zh: 所以，那对联邦调查局来说并不是一个温情脉脉的时期。

sentences.en: I mean, Mueller is revered by, in many quarters, by what he did, but was not a warm and fuzzy manager.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，穆勒因其所作所为在许多方面受到尊崇，但他并不是一个和蔼可亲的管理者。

sentences.en: So at this moment, it is the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 所以当时是21世纪初。

sentences.en: He's starting to transform the
sentences.zh: 他开始改造

sentences.en: FBI, as you've described, everyone in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局，正如你所描述的那样，美国情报界的每个人都专注于如何保护美国免受另一次可怕的恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: intelligence world is focused on how to protect the United States from another one of these horrible terrorist attacks.
sentences.zh: 正如我所记得的，整个美国政府的策略也开始发生变化。

sentences.en: And the tactics are starting to change, as I recall, all around the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了一些什么事情？

sentences.en: government.

sentences.en: What were some of the things that were happening?
sentences.zh: 那正是布什政府决定在海外秘密监狱中抓捕、拘留和审讯恐怖分子或疑似恐怖分子的时刻。

sentences.en: This was the moment where the Bush administration decided it was going to capture, detain, and interrogate terrorists or suspected terrorists overseas in secret prisons.
sentences.zh: 它打算把他们关在关塔那摩。

sentences.en: It was going to hold them in Guantanamo.

sentences.zh: 开始在没有搜查令的情况下进行窃听，并获取美国人谈话的时刻。

sentences.en: to start wiretapping without warrants and picking up conversations of Americans without warrants.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·穆勒的联邦调查局和鲍勃·穆勒本人是如何适应这些新策略的？他对这些策略有多适应？

sentences.en: And how did Bob Mueller's FBI and Bob Mueller fit into these new strategies and how comfortable was he with them?
sentences.zh: 穆勒对中央情报局实施的审讯和引渡计划并不感到舒服。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 我曾参与过所谓的‘强化审讯技术’的黑狱工作。

sentences.en: I was involved at the black sites with the so-called enhanced interrogation techniques.
sentences.zh: 当我们报告了这一点并拒绝参与时，局长基本上把我们撤了回来，他说，我们不干这种事。

sentences.en: And when we reported that and we refused to participate in it, the director basically pulled us back and he said, we don't do this, this kind of things.

sentences.en: And that's why the FBI, you know, was not involved as an organization into any of these so-called enhanced interrogation techniques.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实为联邦调查局划定了一条底线，许多人认为这真正保护了联邦调查局明确的法律界限。

sentences.en: And so he really drew a line in the sand for the FBI that many people feel really preserved the bright legal line for the FBI.

sentences.en: which greatly expanded the government's ability to collect intelligence in ways that civil libertarians still think have gone way too far.
sentences.zh: 但穆勒也划定了界限。

sentences.en: There's one aspect of the broad warrantless wiretapping program that the Justice Department said was unconstitutional and Mueller refused to go along with.

sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是你我谈到过的那个现在很有名的医院病床场景。

sentences.en: Well, this is the now famous hospital bed scene that you and I have talked about.
sentences.zh: 但它一直是从当时的副司法部长吉姆·科姆的角度来讲述的。

sentences.en: But it's always been told from Jim Comey, the deputy attorney general at the time, from his point of view.

sentences.zh: 这是我生命中非常难忘的一段时期，可能是我整个职业生涯中最困难的时刻，而那天晚上可能是我职业生涯中最艰难的一夜。

sentences.en: this was a very memorable period in my life probably the most difficult time in my entire
sentences.zh: 所以我不会忘记。穆勒是联邦调查局局长，他和时任副司法部长的科米听说布什白宫的人要去医院对抗

sentences.en: professional life and that night was probably the most difficult night of my professional life

sentences.en: so it's not something i forget muller was the fbi director and he and comey who was the deputy

sentences.en: think is unconstitutional.

sentences.zh: 那将是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: If the Bush administration didn't back away from its plans to reauthorize this data mining program, then Comey and Mueller were going to quit.
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局局长和副司法部长说我们要辞职。

sentences.en: I couldn't stay if the administration was going to engage in conduct of the Department of Justice, it said, had no legal basis.
sentences.zh: 对于当时的布什来说，失去他们将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: It simply couldn't stay.
sentences.zh: 他退缩了，他们放弃了那个计划。

sentences.en: That would be extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 穆勒局长没有谈论这件事。

sentences.en: The director of the FBI and the deputy attorney general saying we will quit our jobs.
sentences.zh: 直到后来科米提到它，以及布什总统在回忆录中写到它之前，没人知道这件事。

sentences.en: It would have been catastrophic for Bush at that moment to lose them.
sentences.zh: 他想保护联邦调查局免受任何政治压力。

sentences.en: And he blinked and they backed away from that program.
sentences.zh: 所以他这么做了。

sentences.en: Director Mueller did not talk about this.
sentences.zh: 那是他和联邦调查局另外一两个人之间的事情。

sentences.en: Nobody knew about it until Comey mentioned it later and until President Bush wrote about it in his memoir.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个会吹嘘的人。

sentences.en: He wanted to shield the FBI from any political pressure.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个会在公开场合谈论这些事情的人。

sentences.en: So he did this.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢聚光灯。

sentences.en: That was something between him and maybe one or two other people in the FBI.
sentences.zh: 他只关心任务。

sentences.en: He is not a guy to brag.
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局的评价标准不仅在于我们如何有效地破坏和威慑恐怖主义，还在于我们如何保护所有美国人的公民自由和宪法权利，

sentences.en: He is not a person to talk about these things publicly.
sentences.zh: 包括那些希望伤害我们的人。

sentences.en: He does not like the limelight.
sentences.zh: 那么那个病房里的故事到底是什么？

sentences.en: He is just about the mission.
sentences.zh: 这告诉了我们关于穆勒的什么，特别是关于他与权威的关系？

sentences.en: The FBI will be judged not just on how effectively we disrupt and deter terrorism, but also on how we protect the civil liberties and the constitutional rights of all Americans,
sentences.zh: 我认为它真正告诉你的是，穆勒将联邦调查局视为一个特殊的独立场所，并将司法行政和司法部视为独立于政府之外的机构，因为我认为联邦调查局普遍的共识是：我们不属于任何人的阵营。

sentences.en: including those who wish to do us ill.
sentences.zh: 包括那些希望伤害我们的人。

sentences.en: So what is the story in that hospital room?
sentences.zh: 那么那个病房里的故事到底是什么？

sentences.en: What does that tell us about Mueller and in particular about his relationship to authority?
sentences.zh: 这告诉了我们关于穆勒的什么，特别是关于他与权威的关系？

sentences.en: I think what it really tells you is that Mueller views the FBI as a special independent place and views the administration of justice and the Just Department as separate from the administration because I think the prevailing wisdom at the FBI is we're not on anybody's team here.
sentences.zh: 我认为它真正告诉你的是，穆勒将联邦调查局视为一个特殊的独立场所，并将司法行政和司法部视为独立于政府之外的机构，因为我认为联邦调查局普遍的共识是：我们不属于任何人的阵营。

sentences.en: On any given day, we might have to investigate anybody, and we don't want to be buddies with anybody.
sentences.zh: 在任何时候，我们都可能需要调查任何人，而我们不想与任何人称兄道弟。

sentences.en: Do we know why Bob Mueller decided at the seeming end of his career to take this assignment as special counsel in charge of overseeing the investigation into the Trump administration and Russia?
sentences.zh: 我们知道鲍勃·穆勒为什么会在职业生涯看似终结之时，决定接受这项特别检察官的任命，负责监督对特朗普政府和俄罗斯的调查吗？

sentences.en: So true to Bob Mueller form, he has not said anything, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，正如鲍勃·穆勒一贯的作风，他什么都没说，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean that is –
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是——

sentences.en: Anything.
sentences.zh: 什么都没说。

sentences.en: Anything.
sentences.zh: 什么都没说。

sentences.en: That is one of the jokes around Washington.
sentences.zh: 这是华盛顿流传的笑话之一。

sentences.en: I mean, Bob Mueller wouldn't tell you if your shoes were on fire.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就算你的鞋子着火了，鲍勃·穆勒也不会告诉你。

sentences.en: But there aren't many people on the shortlist in Washington who could get this appointment and put both sides at ease and give them confidence that things would go well.
sentences.zh: 但在华盛顿，能获得这项任命、让双方都感到安心并相信事情会顺利进行的人选并不多。

sentences.en: And Bob is one of the most important and respected law enforcement figures in the country.
sentences.zh: 而鲍勃是全国最重要、最受尊敬的执法人物之一。

sentences.en: And so I think there's a sense of duty or a sense of country if you're asked to do something that not a lot of people can do that has high stakes and preserves an institution that you care deeply about.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果你被要求去做一件没多少人能做、风险极高且关乎你深切关心的机构存亡的事，这其中包含着一种责任感或爱国情怀。

sentences.en: I mean that's all in Bob's wheelhouse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这完全在鲍勃的能力范围内。

sentences.en: He will follow the facts.
sentences.zh: 他会追随事实。

sentences.en: And if there's anything, rest assured, he will find it.
sentences.zh: 如果有任何问题，请放心，他一定会查出来。

sentences.en: And I don't think there's anyone in Washington that can deter Robert Mueller from doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为华盛顿没人能阻止罗伯特·穆勒做正确的事。

sentences.en: If you're Donald Trump and you feel this is fake news,
sentences.zh: 如果你是唐纳德·特朗普，并且觉得这是假新闻，

sentences.en: who better to investigate it than somebody who's going to try to remain low-key and isn't going to sensationalize it and is willing to walk away from a case at the end?
sentences.zh: 还有谁比一个行事低调、不会大肆渲染、并且愿意在案件结束时全身而退的人更适合调查它呢？

sentences.en: Now, if there's a problem, I'm not sure I would want Bob Mueller to be the guy investigating me.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果真的出了问题，我不确定我是否希望鲍勃·穆勒来调查我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Of all the congressional investigations into Russian interference in the election, the most influential is overseen by the Senate Intelligence Committee.
sentences.zh: 在所有关于俄罗斯干预选举的国会调查中，最具影响力的是由参议院情报委员会监督的那一项。

sentences.en: Eight of its members are Republican.
sentences.zh: 其成员中有八名是共和党人。

sentences.en: Seven are Democrats.
sentences.zh: 七名是民主党人。

sentences.en: Which is kind of unusual.
sentences.zh: 这有点不寻常。

sentences.en: So, you know, just the movement of a couple senators in either direction can change the balance, which is why these four people are so important.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，仅仅是几位参议员的立场变动就可能改变平衡，这就是为什么这四个人如此重要。

sentences.en: Coral Hulse has identified the four Republican members who he believes could sway the outcome of the committee's investigation.
sentences.zh: 科拉尔·赫尔斯确定了四名他认为可能左右委员会调查结果的共和党成员。

sentences.en: Senator Collins.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯参议员。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，主席先生。

sentences.en: They are Senator Susan Collins of Maine, most moderate Republican in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们是来自缅因州的苏珊·柯林斯参议员，她是参议院中最温和的共和党人。

sentences.en: Is this a recommendation that you believe should be implemented?
sentences.zh: 你认为这项建议应该付诸实施吗？

sentences.en: It's hard to believe we're even having this hearing today discussing this topic.
sentences.zh: 很难相信我们今天竟然还在举行听证会讨论这个话题。

sentences.en: James Lankford, who was a youth minister a long time in his home state, and he sees this effort as part of his calling, really.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·兰克福德，他在家乡做了很长时间的青年牧师，他确实将这项工作视为他使命的一部分。

sentences.en: This is not new for the Russians.
sentences.zh: 这对俄罗斯人来说并不新鲜。

sentences.en: They've done this for a long time across Europe.
sentences.zh: 他们在欧洲各地这样做已经很久了。

sentences.en: Why now?
sentences.zh: 为什么是现在？

sentences.en: I've got about four questions.
sentences.zh: 我大约有四个问题。

sentences.en: Why do you think there was this element of surprise?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么会有这种惊讶的成分？

sentences.en: Roy Blunt, really a veteran senator from Missouri, and is like the consummate congressional dealmaker.
sentences.zh: 罗伊·布朗特，确实是来自密苏里州的资深参议员，就像是国会中完美的交易撮合者。

sentences.en: Marco Rubio, senator from Florida, of course was a presidential candidate, very interested in foreign policy and America's position in the world.
sentences.zh: 马可·鲁比奥，佛罗里达州参议员，当然曾是总统候选人，对外交政策和美国在世界上的地位非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: Was that not their goal?
sentences.zh: 那不是他们的目标吗？

sentences.en: And if it was, have they not largely achieved that based on how this issue has been discussed since the aftermath of the election?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，考虑到选举后人们讨论这个问题的方式，他们难道没有在很大程度上实现了这一目标吗？

sentences.en: And they are sort of serving, from my perspective anyway, as an impetus from the Republican side to keep this thing going and get it to a credible end.
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，他们正在充当共和党方面的推动力，以保持这件事的进展并使其有一个可信的结局。

sentences.en: We are working very hard and we talk a lot with one another as well.
sentences.zh: 我们工作非常努力，而且我们也经常互相交流。

sentences.en: You sat down with Senator Susan Collins.
sentences.zh: 你和苏珊·柯林斯参议员坐下来谈过。

sentences.en: Where did you talk to her?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里和她谈的？

sentences.en: So I talked to her in her personal office.
sentences.zh: 我在她的私人办公室里和她谈的。

sentences.en: And Susan Collins, of course, she's the most moderate Republican in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 当然，苏珊·柯林斯是参议院中最温和的共和党人。

sentences.en: She's almost what you would use to call a liberal Republican, but that doesn't exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 她几乎可以被称为自由派共和党人，但那种人已经不存在了。

sentences.en: Interesting with Senator Collins.
sentences.zh: 关于柯林斯参议员的情况很有趣。

sentences.en: I was a 21-year-old intern during the Watergate summer of 1974.
sentences.zh: 1974年“水门事件”的那个夏天，我是一名21岁的实习生。

sentences.en: She was an intern here for William Cohen, the then-Congressman from Maine,
sentences.zh: 当时她是威廉·科恩的实习生，那是来自缅因州的国会议员，

sentences.en: who as a freshman was on the Judiciary Committee and helped write the articles of impeachment for Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 他作为一年级议员在司法委员会任职，并帮助起草了针对理查德·尼克松的弹劾条款。

sentences.en: So as we say in Washington, this isn't her first rodeo.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我们在华盛顿所说，这已经不是她第一次经历这种阵仗了。

sentences.en: In fact, she'd mentioned it to a younger reporter the other day, and he said, oh, you must mean President Clinton's impeachment.
sentences.zh: 事实上，前几天她向一位年轻记者提到过这件事，他说，哦，你一定是指克林顿总统的弹劾案。

sentences.en: And I said, no.
sentences.zh: 我说，不。

sentences.en: This was before you were born.
sentences.zh: 那是在你出生之前。

sentences.en: She knows from the inside how to conduct congressional investigations.
sentences.zh: 她从内部了解如何进行国会调查。

sentences.en: She was a senior Senate staffer before she ran for office.
sentences.zh: 她在竞选公职之前曾是参议院的高级幕僚。

sentences.en: What did Senator Collins say is the kind of day-to-day work of this?
sentences.zh: 柯林斯参议员说这种日常工作是什么样的？

sentences.en: I mean, what are they actually doing in the Intelligence Committee?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在情报委员会到底在做什么？

sentences.en: How are they going about investigating this?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何着手调查这件事的？

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of a grind, I think.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这是一种苦差事。

sentences.en: It has not been easy to get access to some of the information that we need.
sentences.zh: 要获得我们需要的一些信息并不容易。

sentences.en: The Intelligence Committee has negotiated with the CIA to get access to some extremely sensitive,
sentences.zh: 情报委员会已经与中央情报局进行了谈判，以获取一些极其敏感的、

sentences.en: what we call raw intelligence data, which is, you know, not analyzed by the CIA with a finding, but the actual material they collect.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为原始情报数据的东西，你知道，这不是中央情报局分析后的结论，而是他们收集的实际材料。

sentences.en: And they have to go out to Langley and sit in a room by themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们必须去兰利，独自坐在一个房间里。

sentences.en: I can tell you that I've been three times.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，我已经去过三次了。

sentences.en: And pour through these documents, and there's thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 翻阅这些文件，有成千上万份。

sentences.en: And I've spent many hours going through the raw intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间查阅这些原始情报。

sentences.en: There's a reason why we don't usually get raw intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我们通常不获取原始情报是有原因的。

sentences.en: It's not vetted.
sentences.zh: 它未经审查。

sentences.en: It's not verified.
sentences.zh: 它未经核实。

sentences.en: The source may not be reliable.
sentences.zh: 来源可能不可靠。

sentences.en: So it's been a very interesting exercise.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的练习。

sentences.en: It's one that makes our intelligence agencies very uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这让我们的情报机构感到非常不安。

sentences.en: They want judgment and expertise to be brought to bear.
sentences.zh: 他们希望发挥判断力和专业知识。

sentences.en: But if we're going to get a full picture of what went on, we really need access to those reports.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们想全面了解所发生的事情，我们确实需要查阅这些报告。

sentences.en: This is a complex investigation.
sentences.zh: 这是一项复杂的调查。

sentences.en: And as you pull the threads, you find it's connected to a whole lot of other threads in this tapestry that we're not yet seeing the whole of.
sentences.zh: 当你抽丝剥茧时，你会发现它与这幅挂毯中许多其他我们尚未看清全貌的线索相连。

sentences.en: What did Senator Collins say about the sudden appointment of a special counsel by the Department of Justice and what role that might play in potentially complicating the Senate's own investigation into this?
sentences.zh: 柯林斯参议员对于司法部突然任命特别检察官有何看法？这在多大程度上可能会使参议院对此事的调查复杂化？

sentences.en: When Robert Mueller was appointed, it was sort of a surprise, as you recall.
sentences.zh: 正如你所记得的，罗伯特·穆勒被任命时，这有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I mean, no one was really expecting it that day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那天没人真正预料到这一点。

sentences.en: Democrats had been pushing for a special counsel.
sentences.zh: 民主党人一直在推动任命特别检察官。

sentences.en: And immediately there was concern raised, like, how is what is this going to do to the congressional investigations?
sentences.zh: 而且人们立即提出了担忧，比如，这对国会调查会有什么影响？

sentences.en: And the Intelligence Committee in the Senate is considered the top investigation.
sentences.zh: 参议院情报委员会被认为是最高级别的调查。

sentences.en: They really have the jurisdiction to get at this probably the deepest way possible.
sentences.zh: 他们确实有管辖权，能以最深入的方式查清此事。

sentences.en: I see the appointment of a special counsel as being complementary to the work that we're doing in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我认为任命特别检察官是对我们在参议院所做工作的补充。

sentences.en: Only a special counsel has the authority to file criminal charges if they are found to be warranted.
sentences.zh: 只有特别检察官有权在认为有必要的情况下提出刑事指控。

sentences.en: Only the United States Congress could pass a law that imposed new sanctions on the Russian government if we established their involvement.
sentences.zh: 只有美国国会才能通过法律，在我们确定俄罗斯政府参与的情况下，对其施加新的制裁。

sentences.en: So we have two very separate missions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有两项非常独立的任务。

sentences.en: And they seem to be pretty satisfied that they can continue their work while the FBI and the special counsel do theirs.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎相当满意，认为可以在联邦调查局和特别检察官进行调查的同时继续自己的工作。

sentences.en: What did Senator Collins say about the Republican
sentences.zh: 柯林斯参议员对于共和党

sentences.en: Party investigating one of its own in the White House?
sentences.zh: 调查白宫内部的自己人有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, I did ask her whether or not, you know, she's willing to follow through all the way if it could potentially blow up on her party.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实问过她，如果这可能会让她的党派陷入困境，她是否愿意追查到底。

sentences.en: And she said it, that was her desire.
sentences.zh: 她说，那是她的愿望。

sentences.en: To have allegations that a foreign power tried to interfere with our choice of whom should be the next president of the United States is alarming, to say the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 有指控称外国势力试图干预我们选择谁应成为下一任美国总统，这至少是令人震惊的。

sentences.en: we need to continue our investigation.
sentences.zh: 我们需要继续我们的调查。

sentences.en: We need to follow the evidence wherever it leads.
sentences.zh: 我们需要追随证据，无论它指向哪里。

sentences.en: And this is an issue that is taking up a great deal of my time, but I think it should.
sentences.zh: 这是一个占用我大量时间的问题，但我认为这是应该的。

sentences.en: I think it's that important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: If it turns out it's bad for your side of the aisle, you won't have any problem with that?
sentences.zh: 如果结果对你们党派不利，你也不会有任何问题吗？

sentences.en: I really want to know what happened.
sentences.zh: 我真的想知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: I want to know the truth.
sentences.zh: 我想知道真相。

sentences.en: No matter who is implicated, no matter where the evidence leads.
sentences.zh: 无论涉及谁，无论证据指向哪里。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: He's a great guy, decent guy.
